**Status:** the framing is fixed; the draws are not written yet, so nothing below
is a result.

Take the claim as it is usually stated: two groups, a mean difference of a few
points, the same spread either side. Then draw from it, because nearly every
question people actually argue about is arithmetic on that draw.

## What the draw answers

Three numbers, none of which anyone can do in their head:

- **Overlap.** What fraction of the two distributions sits in the same range, and
  how many of the lower group out-score the median of the upper one.
- **The extremes.** What share of the top and bottom percentiles comes from each
  group, given that the difference in means is small relative to the spread.
- **Reversals.** How often a randomly chosen pair — one from each group — ends up
  ordered against the group means.

## Why simulate rather than argue

The answers move very little from sample to sample. That is the whole point: a
claim about distributions is settled by drawing from distributions, not by
citing the most extreme person anyone has happened to meet. The simulation also
makes the one thing worth saying plain — that a difference in means says almost
nothing about where an individual sits, and a great deal about the far tails.
